paragraph: Leonia's single-family market is a real seller's market right now. Twenty-two homes sold over six months at a median of $887,500, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.04, about 68 percent closing above asking, and a median of 16 days on market. Expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial with two or three baths, and colonials make up the clear majority of what traded. Sales ran from $570,000 to $2.2 million, so the median is the number to anchor on. Condos and townhouses are a much thinner slice at 7 sales and a median of $460,000, splitting roughly evenly between condo units and townhouses, mostly two-bedroom, one-bath. Nothing there sold above asking and the median days on market was 54, so you have room to negotiate and think. On trend, no single month cleared five closings, so there is no monthly signal worth reading here. Work off the six-month picture. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle and lower price point of a condo or townhouse.
